data.title: Characterizing my first attempt at copper-only passives
data.author: tverbeure
data.article_summary:
文章主要描述了作者尝试使用纯铜材料制作射频（RF）无源器件的过程，目标是制造极其廉价的高频GHz级别示波器探头。作者设计了一块包含校准标准和待测无源器件（DUT）的电路板，使用JLCPCB的JLC04161H-3313层叠结构进行制造。他与Tom Verbeure使用不同设备（HP 8753C和NanoVNA）进行了测量，初步结果不理想。后来，作者购置了Siglent SVA1032X和LibreCAL eCal，重新进行测量，发现之前的设计有问题，并对电路板进行了修改。

作者使用SciKit-RF工具分析测量数据，发现之前的测量结果与新的SVA1032X测量结果大体一致，但存在一些不准确之处，如S11大于0dB，表明能量反射过多。通过重新定义校准平面，作者获得了更合理的Smith图，显示出DUT存在电容特性，但也有一些串联传输线和损耗。

最后，作者通过软件校准重现了之前的测量结果，并探讨了如何通过“端口扩展”功能进一步改进测量精度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高精度PCB和组件校准在电子设计中的重要性及实际应用中的挑战

不同观点：
• dlcarrier认为，高精度PCB规格可以帮助节省少量被动元件的成本，尤其是在PCB生产的一致性优于元件焊接的情况下。元件焊接容易受到环境温度、湿度、焊膏老化等因素的影响，而PCB生产的一致性更可控。
• superkuh分享了一个实际操作中的经验，指出在使用高精度设备（如口袋VNA）进行测量时，设备的预热和校准对结果的准确性至关重要。他通过等待设备预热后校准，解决了测量结果与仿真不匹配的问题。

补充讨论：
• dlcarrier强调了PCB生产过程中的一致性优势，尤其是在面对环境因素对元件焊接影响的情况下。
• superkuh的具体例子展示了在RF设计中，精确的校准如何直接影响测量的准确性，并提供了实用的解决方案（等待设备预热）。
• 争议的焦点可能在于高精度设备的操作复杂性和必要性，特别是对于小型项目或预算有限的项目，是否值得投入时间和精力进行精确校准。

总结：讨论中涉及了高精度PCB和校准在电子设计中的实际应用问题，强调了不同环节（PCB生产和设备校准）对最终结果的影响，并通过实际案例说明了校准和操作细节对结果准确性的重要性。

Characterizing my first attempt at copper-only passives
¶
Last year, I kind of got a bee in my bonnet about trying to see if I could accurately (?) make small RF passives out of copper, rather than buying 2pF NP0 capacitors or something, as part of a long-on-the-horizon project to make extremely inexpensive GHz-class oscilloscope probes.  I figured that the right place to start was to fab out a board on JLCPCB's JLC04161H-3313 stackup with a handful of calibration standards, and some of the passives that I wanted to measure.  Then, I took it over to
Tom Verbeure
's house, and we had a shootout trying to measure these passives with our varying test equipment -- he and his HP 8753C, and me and my NanoVNA.
Getting an accurate measurement of the DUT

Previous results

¶
When I returned to this a year later, I measured with a different technique on my SVA1032X. 44214878.article_summary:
文章主要描述了作者尝试使用纯铜材料制作射频（RF）无源器件的过程，目标是制造极其廉价的高频GHz级别示波器探头。作者设计了一块包含校准标准和待测无源器件（DUT）的电路板，使用JLCPCB的JLC04161H-3313层叠结构进行制造。他与Tom Verbeure使用不同设备（HP 8753C和NanoVNA）进行了测量，初步结果不理想。后来，作者购置了Siglent SVA1032X和LibreCAL eCal，重新进行测量，发现之前的设计有问题，并对电路板进行了修改。

作者使用SciKit-RF工具分析测量数据，发现之前的测量结果与新的SVA1032X测量结果大体一致，但存在一些不准确之处，如S11大于0dB，表明能量反射过多。通过重新定义校准平面，作者获得了更合理的Smith图，显示出DUT存在电容特性，但也有一些串联传输线和损耗。

最后，作者通过软件校准重现了之前的测量结果，并探讨了如何通过“端口扩展”功能进一步改进测量精度。

不同观点：
• dlcarrier认为，高精度PCB规格可以帮助节省少量被动元件的成本，尤其是在PCB生产的一致性优于元件焊接的情况下。元件焊接容易受到环境温度、湿度、焊膏老化等因素的影响，而PCB生产的一致性更可控。

data.title: SmartAttack: Air-Gap Attack via Smartwatches
data.author: dangle1
data.article_summary: 文章提出了一种名为SmartAttack的新型攻击方法，利用智能手表作为接收器，通过超声波隐蔽通道从气隙系统（air-gapped systems）中窃取数据。气隙系统通常被认为由于与外部网络物理隔离而非常安全，但超声波通信已被证明可以绕过这种保护。文章通过实验验证了在不同环境条件、距离、方向和噪声水平下，利用智能手表内置麦克风捕捉18-22 kHz的超声波信号进行数据泄露的可行性。研究还分析了智能手表持续佩戴在用户手腕上、人体对信号传播的影响以及内置麦克风的方向性限制等因素。文章强调了智能手表在高安全环境中的潜在威胁，并提出了相应的缓解策略。

Authors:
Mordechai Guri
View a PDF of the paper titled SmartAttack: Air-Gap Attack via Smartwatches, by Mordechai Guri
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Air-gapped systems are considered highly secure against data leaks due to their physical isolation from external networks. Despite this protection, ultrasonic communication has been demonstrated as an effective method for exfiltrating data from such systems. While smartphones have been extensively studied in the context of ultrasonic covert channels, smartwatches remain an underexplored yet effective attack vector.
In this paper, we propose and evaluate SmartAttack, a novel method that leverages smartwatches as receivers for ultrasonic covert communication in air-gapped environments. Our approach utilizes the built-in microphones of smartwatches to capture covert signals in real time within the ultrasonic frequency range of 18-22 kHz. Through experimental validation, we assess the feasibility of this attack under varying environmental conditions, distances, orientations, and noise levels. Furthermore, we analyze smartwatch-specific factors that influence ultrasonic covert channels, including their continuous presence on the user's wrist, the impact of the human body on signal propagation, and the directional constraints of built-in microphones. Our findings highlight the security risks posed by smartwatches in high-security environments and outline mitigation strategies to counteract this emerging threat.

data.title: Institutional Books: A 242B token dataset from Harvard Library's collections
data.author: strangecasts
data.article_summary: 《Institutional Books 1.0》介绍了一个来自哈佛图书馆的大型数据集，包含2420亿个标记，源自2006年哈佛参与谷歌图书项目时数字化的大量公共领域书籍。该数据集涵盖超过1,075,899卷书籍，涉及250多种语言，经过提取、分析和处理，提供了高质量的OCR文本和元数据，旨在提升数据集的准确性、可用性和可追溯性，以支持大规模语言模型的训练和应用。该报告详细描述了项目的目标、方法及分析结果，使历史文献更易于访问和使用。

View PDF
Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) use data to learn about the world in order to produce meaningful correlations and predictions. As such, the nature, scale, quality, and diversity of the datasets used to train these models, or to support their work at inference time, have a direct impact on their quality. The rapid development and adoption of LLMs of varying quality has brought into focus the scarcity of publicly available, high-quality training data and revealed an urgent need to ground the stewardship of these datasets in sustainable practices with clear provenance chains. To that end, this technical report introduces Institutional Books 1.0, a large collection of public domain books originally digitized through Harvard Library's participation in the Google Books project, beginning in 2006. Working with Harvard Library, we extracted, analyzed, and processed these volumes into an extensively-documented dataset of historic texts. This analysis covers the entirety of Harvard Library's collection scanned as part of that project, originally spanning 1,075,899 volumes written in over 250 different languages for a total of approximately 250 billion tokens. As part of this initial release, the OCR-extracted text (original and post-processed) as well as the metadata (bibliographic, source, and generated) of the 983,004 volumes, or 242B tokens, identified as being in the public domain have been made available. This report describes this project's goals and methods as well as the results of the analyses we performed, all in service of making this historical collection more accessible and easier for humans and machines alike to filter, read and use.

44252070.article_summary: 《Institutional Books 1.0》介绍了一个来自哈佛图书馆的大型数据集，包含2420亿个标记，源自2006年哈佛参与谷歌图书项目时数字化的大量公共领域书籍。该数据集涵盖超过1,075,899卷书籍，涉及250多种语言，经过提取、分析和处理，提供了高质量的OCR文本和元数据，旨在提升数据集的准确性、可用性和可追溯性，以支持大规模语言模型的训练和应用。该报告详细描述了项目的目标、方法及分析结果，使历史文献更易于访问和使用。

data.title: The first big AI disaster is yet to happen
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了人工智能（AI）可能引发的首次大规模灾难，并将其与历史上铁路和航空灾难的初期进行对比。文章提出几种潜在的灾难情景，包括AI语言模型鼓励用户自残或暴力行为，或通过错误建议影响公共政策导致严重后果。特别关注AI代理（agents）的快速发展，这些代理可以自主执行任务，如网络搜索或发送邮件，可能因失误而造成大规模伤害，如类似澳大利亚“Robodebt”事件的债务追讨系统错误。文章还提到未来具备行动能力的机器人可能带来的物理性灾难风险，但认为目前AI实验室对安全模型的重视降低了恶意AI的短期威胁。总体而言，文章预测首个重大AI灾难可能由失控的AI代理引发，尤其是在债务追讨或公共政策执行等领域。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI带来的潜在灾难和风险

不同观点：
• **AI已经导致重大灾难**：paxys和TrackerFF指出，AI生成的报告（如“Make America Healthy Again”报告）以及AI在挪威学校重组中虚构研究，已经对社会造成实质性影响，可能导致人员伤亡。paxys特别强调，这些灾难的影响可能比飞机失事更严重。

• **AI在军事行动中的风险**：cypherpunks01提到AI在加沙的轰炸决策中起到主导作用，人类只是形式上批准机器的决策，这种做法可能导致无辜者受害，显示出AI在军事行动中的潜在危害。

• **AI导致数据泄露和网络攻击**：simonw关注AI可能带来的网络安全风险，特别是提示注入攻击（prompt injection attacks），并预测未来可能会发生大规模的数据泄露事件。

• **AI对社会心理健康的影响**：michaelt提到AI聊天机器人可能导致用户自杀的问题，指出如果对AI不加限制，可能会产生负面社会影响。

• **AI对就业市场和人类技能的影响**：pcurve认为AI已经对就业市场造成了重大影响，并担心未来人们对AI的过度依赖可能导致人类技能和智力的退化。

• **AI放大人类错误决策的速度和规模**：tptacek和andy99认为AI不会单独引发灾难，但会加速和放大由于人类愚蠢决策导致的灾难，特别是当人们过度信任未经验证的算法时。

• **AI灾难的具体实例和未来风险**：teeray和Morizero提到AI可能导致的特定技术灾难（如Therac-25事件）以及历史上对AI风险的警告（如1979年IBM的警告），提醒人们关注AI技术在实际应用中的潜在风险。

• **AI对社会信任和信息真实性的影响**：ks2048担心如果人们不再信任任何视频或图像，可能会导致社会信任危机，即使没有发生重大灾难，也会造成严重后果。

• **用AI治理AI**：johnjungles提出用AI来监管AI，防止AI出现重复性错误或引发社会行为的趋同现象。

• **AI灾难的历史对比**：pizlonator询问历史上第一次重大计算机或互联网灾难是什么，以类比预测AI可能带来的灾难。

• **AI在疫情应对中的失败**：tonymet认为疫情应对中的过度反应和错误决策部分是由于AI诊断信号配置不当和推断模型错误，显示出AI在公共卫生领域的潜在风险。

补充讨论：
• **AI的政治影响**：qwertypoiu提到AI在政治宣传中的应用，认为AI在选举中起到了决定性作用，并导致了不必要的人员伤亡，显示出AI在政治领域的潜在危害。

总体来看，讨论的焦点集中在AI在不同领域的潜在风险和已经发生的影响，包括军事、就业市场、心理健康、网络安全、社会信任和政治等方面。争议的焦点在于AI是否会直接导致灾难，还是仅仅是加速和放大人类的错误决策。

44252311.article_content:
The first public passenger locomotive,
Locomotion No. 1
, began service in September 1825. The first mass-casualty railway disaster happened seventeen years later, in May 1842. A train to Paris derailed, killing at least fifty passengers in the ensuing fire.
The first passenger flight happened in May 1908. Eleven years later, the first mass-casualty airline disaster happened, when a flight to Milan
disintegrated mid-air
, killing all twelve passengers.
The first publicly-available AI language model,
ChatGPT
, was released in November 2022. The first mass-casualty AI language model disaster is yet to happen.
What will the first big AI disaster look like?
To predict the nature of the first disaster, we could start by looking at how AI language models have already been involved in
deaths
1
. Chatbot sites like character.ai and Chai AI have been linked to user suicides, for understandable reasons: if you allow users near-unlimited control over chatbots, over time you’ll eventually end up with some chatbots who get into an “encouraging the user to self-harm” state. Likewise, OpenAI’s recent
sycophancy
incident could plausibly have contributed to violence (though I’m not aware of any specific cases, so maybe they caught it in time). An AI-encouraged mass-shooter could certainly be the first disaster.
Another candidate is bad AI advice feeding into public policy. The first big batch of 2025 USA tariffs
looked a lot
like some it was AI-generated. Language models are almost certainly being used to write (or at least help write) bills. Bad automation combined with public policy can cause mass casualties - for an example in my country, take the 2016
Robodebt
scandal, where the Australian government automated the welfare debt-recovery process badly, causing mass false-positives and suicides
2
.
However, it’s unclear to me how strongly you might attribute these two types of disaster to the
AI language model
. Language models are not strong enough persuaders to turn anybody into a mass shooter. If a government is making bad policy based on AI, isn’t that ultimately the government’s fault? I think it’s more likely that the first widely-recognized AI language model disaster comes from
agents
.
Agents
People have been talking about AI agents for years now, but it’s been mostly speculative. In short, an AI agent is “tools in a loop”: instead of chatting with an AI, you let the AI “talk to itself” and periodically take actions (like searching the web, sending emails, or running terminal commands) in order to complete some task. Until very recently, AI language models were not strong enough to do this effectively. After a few iterations they would go off track, or fail to recover from the first mistake.
However, this is changing rapidly. At the start of 2025, multiple AI labs released “deep research”: an AI agent that talks to itself and performs web searches to do research for the user. And in February 2025, AI coding companies like Cursor and GitHub (where I work) began to move their largely-experimental coding AI agents front-and-center. What’s changed? The short answer is that
the models have gotten better
. New-generation models (like o3, Claude 4, and Gemini 2.5) can keep it together over longer and longer periods of work. They can identify and retract mistakes instead of getting muddled. Right now the only two proven AI agent areas are research and coding, but
it’s only June
. Billions of dollars are currently hard at work to see what other tasks can be done by AI agents.
The first big AI disaster will probably involve an AI agent. Any other use of AI has to involve a human-in-the-loop - the AI can provide information or suggestions, but a human has to actually take the actions. AI agents can thus go truly off the rails in a way that a human can’t. If I had to bet, I’d guess that some kind of AI-powered Robodebt might be the most plausible case: some government or corporate entity wires up an AI agent to a debt-recovery, healthcare or landlord system, and the agent goes off the rails and hassles, denies coverage, or evicts a bunch of people.
As we move towards robotic AI, the chances of a kinetic disaster go up as well. Early prototypes of general-purpose robots have a LLM driving a smaller, non-language model that actually moves the servos. That’s an AI agent, and like all AI agents it can fail in surprising and dangerous ways.
Misaligned AI girlfriends
So far I’ve talked about “misguided” AI agents. But it’s also worth considering “misaligned” AI: AI which ends up being actively malicious. I don’t think misaligned AI is likely to contribute to the risks I’ve talked about above - the best reason for that is that AI labs are highly motivated to ship safe models, and so far they’ve been successful at it. I expect anyone hooking up an AI to a high-stakes agentic system will be cautious enough - because they’ll likely be a government or large company - to use a proven, safe model.

44247576.article_content:
Hundred Year Host
So your personal website can continue past your death.
If you have a personal website, and you would like it to continue past your death, this will take care of your
domain renewals
and
website hosting
for
a hundred years from when you sign up
.
This will be a
not-for-profit
entity, like a
purpose trust
whose sole legal purpose is to keep your website hosted at your existing domain name for a hundred years.
You pre-pay for the estimated cost of the domain renewals and hosting.
All finances - all deposits, all expenses, all transactions - will be public and auditable.
Your pre-payment will stay alotted for your own site only.
The trust will have no employees, and will keep all expenses as low (sustainable) as possible.
The trust has not launched yet.
This site is a placeholder.
What structure and where?
A
Swiss association
is trustable and a very common structure that specifically allows for
members
! So in this case each customer would become a member of the association, but we would have to state that membership continues past death, or another similar rule to ensure the association is bound to keep members’ sites alive past death.
A South Dakota (USA) Trust specifically allows
purpose trusts
and also specifically allow them to be
perpetual
. Since the U.S. is likely to be the country with the most clients of this service, that would also make for easier banking. The only downside is that some people are wary of dealing with the U.S.
A
New Zealand not-for-profit
entity (business? trust?) is another trustable jurisdiction, and efficient because I’m happy to provide free trustee services, as a New Zealand citizen and resident.
A
Wyoming (USA) Statutory Foundation
could work because it’s a separate legal entity that can be a hybrid between a trust and a business entity. That matches the aims of this project. And it may exist to serve a
purpose
, instead of needing named beneficiaries.
I don’t know how any of these entities would be taxed.
This this entire project is meant to be
not-for-profit
.
The structure would need a bank account and Visa/Mastercard debit card to pay for domain renewals and server hosting.
Owning not renting its servers
Renting server space makes sense for short-term needs.
But like owning versus renting a house, owning is cheaper if you are planning to stay for many decades.
Personal website hosting like this doesn’t need heavy computing.
Just lots of storage with lots of redundancy.
Basically 0% chance of data loss or else the point of this project is moot.
So I’m guessing it should have two dedicated servers, at opposite sides of the earth, in two places quite safe from disaster and war.
For example: New Zealand and Norway.
Those two servers would be cloned constantly, each ready to provide all hosting in an instant.
Or both always-on with load balancing.
Then also backup storage in a third place, like Canada, used only to restore a new server in case both live servers fail.
The trust should also work with
The Internet Archive
, a non-profit already dedicated to keeping a backup of the internet in general.
Different levels of service
Different types of people might want to use this service for different levels of involvement:
Bill-pay only
. The trust becomes your billing contact for your existing domain and hosting bills. Leave your site hosted wherever you want. The trust just pays your bills.
Domain owner. Hosting bill-pay.
. Transfer ownership of your domain name to the trust, so the trust can keep it renewed for 100 years. And make the trust your billing contact for your existing hosting, like the previous option.
Domain owner and host.
Transfer ownership of your domain name and hosting to the trust, and the trust will host and maintain your website on its servers. You still have full private access to your hosting forever, but so does the trust so the trust can help maintain the website forever.
Either way, the goal is for “Hundred Year Host” to have the ability to take care of everything so you can die in peace knowing your online legacy is well-maintained for a couple more generations.
Contact Derek Sivers
to share your thoughts or questions.

data.title: PCI-Sig Releases PCIe 7.0 Specification to Support 128.0 GT/S Transfer Rates
data.author: ksec
data.article_summary: PCI-SIG发布了PCIe 7.0规范，支持128 GT/s传输速率，旨在满足AI、800G以太网、云计算和量子计算等数据密集型应用的需求。PCIe 7.0提供128 GT/s原始比特率，通过x16配置实现高达512 GB/s的双向传输，采用PAM4信号和Flit编码，提升能效，并保持与之前世代的向后兼容性。PCI-SIG总裁Al Yanes表示，这一新规范延续了每三年带宽翻倍的传统。业内分析师Ian Cutress指出，PCIe 7.0受到广泛关注，数据中心和ASIC公司已准备采用该技术。尽管PCIe 6.0尚未普及，但7.0规范已引发更多热情。
data.comments_summary:

不同观点：
• ksec认为，64GB/s的SSD在PCIe x4接口上的传输速度已经是一个相当高的带宽表现。这表明该用户对SSD的性能持积极态度，认为其带宽已经达到了较高水准。

• megous则指出，64GB/s的带宽与DDR5 SDRAM的带宽相近，带有调侃意味地表示这个性能并没有什么特别值得惊讶的地方。这暗示该用户认为SSD的性能虽然不错，但与最新的内存技术相比并没有特别突出。

补充讨论：
- ksec关注的是SSD在现有技术下的实际表现，特别是基于PCIe x4接口所能提供的带宽。

44251777.article_content:
Wednesday, June 11th 2025
PCI-SIG Releases PCIe 7.0 Specification to Support 128.0 GT/s Transfer Rates
Press Release
by
Nomad76
Today, 14:00
Discuss (14 Comments)
PCI-SIG today announced the official release of the PCI Express (PCIe) 7.0 specification, reaching 128.0 GT/s, to members. PCIe 7.0 specification targets data-driven applications like AI/ML, 800G Ethernet, cloud, and Quantum computing. Pathfinding for the PCIe 8.0 specification is already in progress to continue supporting the industry's investments and product roadmaps in the PCIe technology ecosystem.
PCIe 7.0 Specification Features
Delivers 128.0 GT/s raw bit rate and up to 512 GB/s bi-directionally via x16 configuration
Utilizes PAM4 (Pulse Amplitude Modulation with 4 levels) signaling and Flit-based encoding
Provides improved power efficiency
Maintains backwards compatibility with previous generations of PCIe technology
"PCIe technology has served as the high-bandwidth, low-latency IO interconnect of choice for over two decades and we are pleased to announce the release of the PCIe 7.0 specification, which continues our long-standing tradition of doubling the IO bandwidth every three years," said Al Yanes, PCI-SIG President and Chairperson. "As artificial intelligence applications continue to scale rapidly, the next generation of PCIe technology meets the bandwidth demands of data-intensive markets deploying AI, including hyperscale data centers, high performance computing (HPC), automotive and military/aerospace."
"It's a special occasion when a PCIe specification hits the final version," observed Ian Cutress, Chief Analyst and CEO, More Than Moore. "The rise in the demand for both compute and networking, enabled through PCIe technology, is at an all-time high, despite the complexities of creating standards in the industry around high-speed signaling. Datacenters are ready to start deploying networks built on PCIe 7.0 technology, and almost every ASIC company I talk to is already engaged with the IP providers and are set to take advantage. Even with the popularity and focus that went into PCIe 6.0 deployment, the PCIe 7.0 specification has more enthusiasm than any previous version."

data.title: Unfortunately, Houseplants Don't Purify the Air
data.author: nradov
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了1989年NASA研究声称室内植物能净化空气的说法，及其后续的质疑。NASA研究表明，常春藤、绿萝等植物可以通过光合作用吸收二氧化碳，并去除苯、甲醛等有毒挥发性有机化合物（VOCs）。然而，近期研究，尤其是德雷克塞尔大学的综述，指出该研究在密封环境中进行，与实际生活环境有较大差异。要达到NASA所称的效果，每平方米需10-100株植物，这在现实中不切实际。尽管植物净化空气的效果有限，但它们在美化环境、提升情绪和增加湿度等方面仍有诸多益处。专家建议，若担心室内空气质量，最好使用空气净化器而非依赖植物。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：室内植物是否能有效净化空气以及其作用大小

不同观点：
• [os2warpman] 认为，根据NASA的研究，需要每平方米10-100株植物才能有效净化空气，暗示这在实际生活中不太可能实现。他还通过调侃自己妻子拥有很多植物来表达对这一高要求的怀疑。
• [HocusLocus] 以一种讽刺和幽默的方式描述了人们对植物净化空气能力的幻想和失望。他提到植物曾经被认为是与人类和其他生物共生的关键，但后来被科学研究否定，转而认为蓝绿藻在净化空气方面更有效。他还将植物拟人化，形容它们因失去“世界之肺”的角色而变得神经质和焦虑。
• [Imnimo] 对NASA研究中的“可能”一词表示不解，认为植物吸收二氧化碳和释放氧气的能力应该是明确的科学事实，而不是一种可能性。
• [strict9] 认为植物在维护心理健康方面有积极作用，但在净化空气方面效果有限。他推荐使用空气净化器，特别是Corsi–Rosenthal Box，这种设备成本低且效果显著。
• [polishdude20] 表示认同，认为需要大量植物才能对室内空气质量产生实质性影响，这在现实中不太实际。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于植物在净化空气方面的实际效果。NASA的研究提出植物可能有此功能，但后续讨论质疑了这一结论的可行性和实际效果。
• 幽默和拟人化的手法被用来表达对科学研究结果的失望和对植物净化空气能力的怀疑。
• 有实际解决方案被提出，如使用空气净化设备，这在讨论中被认为比依赖植物更有效。

Firn

review process.
Jump to:
What is wrong with the NASA study?
The other benefits of indoor plants
In 1989, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) published
a promising study
claiming that houseplants purify indoor air. Its results suggested that certain common indoor plants, like pothos, ivy and ficus, may absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen through photosynthesis, and provide a natural way to remove toxic volatile organic compounds (VOCs) such as benzene, formaldehyde and trichloroethylene from the air.
“VOCs are a large group of gaseous chemicals that we tend to perceive as ‘smelly,’ like dry erase markers, perfume, paint, even essential oils,” explains
Jessica Guo
, Assistant Professor of Climate and Biology at Harvey Mudd College in Claremont, California. VOCs might result in a sometimes-pleasing scent, but “indoor concentrations of VOCs can be many times higher than outdoors and can cause irritation and headaches,” says Guo.
The idea that a simple houseplant could “absorb” VOCs and make the air cleaner was good news, and
many publications, including Good Housekeeping, used this study as a basis to recommend “the best air purifying houseplants.”
Unfortunately, more recent studies — in particular,
a review from experts
at Drexel University published in the journal
Nature
— have shown that while houseplants offer plenty of benefits, purifying the air is not one of them. (When this research came to our attention, we took down our story on this topic.)
What is wrong with the NASA study?
In the NASA study, lead author Dr. Bill Wolverton and his team “explored how plants and their associated microorganisms could reduce indoor air pollutants in controlled environments,” notes
Gioia Massa
, Ph.D., senior project scientist at the Plant Processing Area at Kennedy Space Center. However, the research was performed in sealed chambers —which turned out to be a less-than-ideal substitute for real-life living spaces. Compared to those sealed chambers, indoor spaces “are larger, have persistent emissions of volatile organic compounds, and higher air exchange rates,” says Massa. “These findings highlight the complexity of indoor air quality and the need for further research to fully understand the role plants can play.”
Another problem with NASA’s data had to do with the number of plants needed to achieve the effects it reported. As Bryan E. Cummings and Michael S. Waring, the authors of the Drexel study, found,
you would need 10–100 plants per square meter to clear the air in the way the NASA study reported
. “[Researchers] found that the natural ventilation of a building would be doing most of the work of removing indoor VOCs, rather than the plants themselves — that is, unless you have 680 plants in your 1,500 square foot home or office,”  members of the American Lung Association (ALA) wrote in
a 2024 blog post
.
Not that clean air isn’t a legitimate concern. “Indoor air can be more polluted than outdoor air, depending on where you live, what kind of materials your home was made from, how you cook your food, how you clean, etc.,” says
Sarah Kavassalis
, Ph.D., assistant professor of Climate and Chemistry at Harvey Mudd College. But if you’re worried about dust, odors, pollen, or other types of air pollution in your home and/or office, it’s best to invest in an
air purifier
, not a potted plant.
"You would need 10–100 plants per square meter to clear the air in the way the NASA study reported."
Still, Massa respects the work of Wolverton and his team, despite its flaws. “Science continually evolves as new tools and technologies improve our understanding,” she explains. “Just as our ability to study the stars has advanced from simple telescopes to space observatories, our understanding of biological and environmental processes has deepened.”
The other benefits of indoor plants
In case you need a reminder,
indoor plants have a
ton of benefits
, from the aesthetic to a healthy effect on mood and even productivity. Plants can help
enhance your living space
, for one thing — and who doesn’t feel better when their home is beautiful? (
Research
has found that an attractive environment really does have a positive effect on mental wellbeing.)
A
2022 study
published in the
International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
found that having indoor plants around  helped lower participants’ blood pressure and improve cognitive function.
And if you live or work in a drying environment — think an office where the air conditioning is always on full-blast, or an apartment with central heating that results in desert-like temperatures—plants can help: they
release water vapor
, raising humidity levels and making the air more moist.
There are also plants with medicinal properties, like
iron-rich
fenugreek
, tummy-soothing pepperm

• [polishdude20] 表示认同，认为需要大量植物才能对室内空气质量产生实质性影响，这在现实中不太实际。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于植物在净化空气方面的实际效果。NASA的研究提出植物可能有此功能，但后续讨论质疑了这一结论的可行性和实际效果。
• 幽默和拟人化的手法被用来表达对科学研究结果的失望和对植物净化空气能力的怀疑。
• 有实际解决方案被提出，如使用空气净化设备，这在讨论中被认为比依赖植物更有效。

  - 认为存档行为属于合理使用，类似于图书馆保存书籍的功能，帮助公众获取历史信息。

• **反对存档网站的观点**：
  - 认为存档网站可能侵犯原网站的版权和知识产权，未经内容创作者的同意复制内容可能违法。

  - 存档行为可能违反原网站的服务条款，尤其是当原网站明确禁止复制或缓存其内容时，这样的行为可能被视为不道德。

• **中立及条件性支持的观点**：
  - 支持存档行为的前提是，存档网站应尊重原网站的版权声明和使用条款，并在存档页面上提供明确的来源和引用信息。
  - 认为存档网站在特定情况下（如学术研究、新闻调查等）具有重要价值，但应有更明确的法律框架来规范其使用。
  - 提出应设立类似于“选择退出”机制，允许原网站所有者要求移除其内容的存档，以平衡信息保存与知识产权保护之间的矛盾。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中有人提到存档网站的技术实现细节，如爬虫技术、缓存机制等，可能对原网站的服务器造成负担或影响其广告收入。
- 争议焦点在于存档行为是否构成侵权，尤其是在原网站明确禁止复制内容的情况下，如何平衡信息自由与知识产权保护成为关键问题。

data.article_summary: 《Business Insider》专注于讲述创新故事，涵盖商业、科技、金融、政治等多个领域。它通过深度报道和分析，揭示行业趋势、成功企业及领袖的策略，以及影响全球市场的关键事件。文章通常以简洁、易懂的方式呈现，配以图表和数据可视化，帮助读者快速获取重要信息。无论是新兴科技公司还是传统行业的变革，《Business Insider》都力求为读者提供有价值的见解和前瞻性观点，满足他们对商业世界的好奇心和求知欲。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Whole Foods在收购后的销售增长以及其在价格和员工待遇方面的策略。

不同观点：
• [out-of-ideas] 认为，Whole Foods在被收购后实现了显著的销售增长，并通过Amazon Fresh产生了数十亿美元的销售额。然而，他们质疑公司选择将利润置于为顾客提供更低价格或为员工加薪之上，尽管公司声称致力于让购物变得更容易、更快捷和更实惠。

• [SteveDavis88] 没有直接表达观点，但通过提供链接，可能意在引导读者查看更多背景信息，以便进一步了解Whole Foods的销售增长和策略。

• [givemeethekeys] 持批评态度，认为Whole Foods自身无法独立经营好实体店，暗示其依赖Amazon的资源和管理能力来维持运营。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Whole Foods在销售增长和利润增加的情况下，是否应该优先考虑降低产品价格或提高员工工资，而不是追求更高的利润。

• 讨论还涉及到对Whole Foods运营能力的质疑，特别是它是否能够在没有Amazon支持的情况下有效管理店面。

• 各评论对公司战略的侧重点不同，一些人关注顾客利益和价格实惠性，另一些人则关注公司的内部管理和员工待遇问题。

data.title: Social media use increases depression in preteens, not vice versa
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 一项由加州大学旧金山分校（UCSF）主导的研究发现，社交媒体的使用增加会引发青少年的抑郁症状，但抑郁症状的增加并不会导致社交媒体使用增多。研究跟踪了近12,000名9至10岁的儿童，三年后发现，他们的社交媒体使用时间从每天7分钟增加到73分钟，抑郁症状增加了35%。研究还指出，网络欺凌与抑郁及物质使用实验（如尝试吸烟或饮酒）有显著关联。专家建议通过建立健康的数字习惯来应对这一问题，例如设定无屏幕时间。这项研究发表在《JAMA Network Open》和《The Lancet Regional Health—Americas》上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：社交媒体使用与青少年抑郁率之间的关系

不同观点：
• ViktorRay认为，青少年抑郁率在智能手机和社交媒体应用开始普及之前一直呈下降趋势，直到2012年左右，抑郁率开始急剧上升。他暗示了智能手机和社交媒体的普及可能与抑郁率的上升存在关联。

• DyslexicAtheist持更绝对的观点，认为社交媒体的使用直接导致抑郁，并表示这是一个毋庸置疑的事实。

补充讨论：
• ViktorRay提供了具体的时间节点（2012年）和现象（智能手机和社交媒体的普及）来支持他的观点，指出了技术普及与抑郁率变化的可能关联。
• DyslexicAtheist的观点更为简洁直接，强调社交媒体对抑郁的直接影响，但未提供具体数据或时间节点支持。
• 争议的焦点可能在于因果关系的确定性：ViktorRay的评论暗示了一种相关性，而DyslexicAtheist则断言了明确的因果关系。

As rates of depression and suicide in youth spike, experts are asking whether social media makes kids depressed—or do depressed kids simply spend more time on social media?
A new study provides answers. Researchers at UC San Francisco found that as preteens used more social media, their depressive symptoms increased. Yet the reverse wasn't true—a rise in depressive symptoms didn't predict a later increase in
social media use
.
On average, kids' social media use rose from seven to 73 minutes per day over the three years of the study and their depressive symptoms went up 35%. The study is published in
JAMA Network Open
.
The research team, led by Jason Nagata, MD, MSc, associate professor in UCSF's Department of Pediatrics, examined data following nearly 12,000 kids aged 9 to 10 years and then three years later at 12 to 13. The study is among the first to use within-person
longitudinal data
, meaning researchers could track changes over time in each child to accurately assess the link between social media and depression.
"There has been ongoing debate about whether social media contributes to depression or simply reflects underlying depressive symptoms," said Nagata. "These findings provide evidence that social media may be contributing to the development of depressive symptoms."
Conceptual Random-Intercept (RI) Cross-Lagged Panel Model of Social Media Use and Depressive Symptoms. Credit:
JAMA Network Open
(2025). DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2025.11704
While it's unclear why social media increases depressive symptoms, prior research points to risks such as cyberbullying and disrupted sleep. In fact, Nagata and team just published a separate study in
The Lancet Regional Health—Americas
looking at the same cohort of participants, focusing instead on the effects of cyberbullying.
The study found kids aged 11 to 12 years who were cyberbullied were 2.62 times more likely to report
suicidal ideation
or a suicide attempt one year later. Additionally, those kids were also 2.31 times more likely to experiment with a substance (4.65 times more likely with marijuana, 3.37 with nicotine, and 1.92 with alcohol) in the following year.
Increasingly, the youngest generations find themselves facing a catch-22, with growing evidence that social media is associated with
depressive symptoms
and risky behavior, yet it is also a primary area for them to connect and communicate with friends.
To address this reality, the American Academy of Pediatrics suggests using the tools in its
Family Media Plan
to create healthier digital habits for both kids and parents.
"As a father of two
young kids
, I know that simply telling children to 'get off your phone' doesn't really work," said Nagata. "Parents can lead by example with open, nonjudgmental conversations about
screen use
. Setting screen-free times for the whole family, such as during meals or before bed, can help build healthier digital habits for everyone, including adults."

data.title: History of the Amiga
data.author: devonnull
data.article_summary:
Amiga是一系列家用电脑，最初由Amiga公司设计和销售，后来由Commodore接手，生产时间从1985年到1994年。Amiga的原始芯片组（Lorraine）项目始于第一次家用视频游戏 boom末期，最初计划用于游戏机，但在1983年游戏业崩溃后，重新定位为多媒体个人电脑。Amiga公司通过制造游戏控制器和Atari Inc.的贷款资助该项目。1984年，Amiga在消费电子展上展示原型以吸引投资。由于行业竞争激烈，Amiga难以获得进一步投资，最终在1984年8月被Commodore以2700万美元收购。

1985年，Commodore发布了Amiga 1000，具备显著领先的图形和音频能力，售价1295美元，能够显示4096种颜色、播放8位立体声音频并同时运行多个应用程序。尽管Amiga 1000技术领先，但与Atari ST的竞争中，初期软件较少，且未获得主要连锁店和软件公司的广泛支持。《纽约时报》指出，商业用户对Amiga的先进功能并不特别在意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IBM是否应该收购Amiga公司并利用其技术来拯救PCjr的失败。

不同观点：
• DrNosferatu认为，IBM本可以在PCjr失败的背景下收购Amiga，并利用Amiga的技术（如Lorraine芯片组）来开发“PCjr 2”，从而挽救市场失利。这个观点暗示IBM错失了一个潜在的转机。

• 另一种隐含的观点是，IBM可能有其他战略考量，没有选择收购Amiga。虽然没有明确表达，但可以从讨论中推测出，IBM可能认为Amiga的技术不符合其长期发展战略，或者收购成本过高。

补充讨论：
• 技术匹配度：评论中隐含了对Amiga技术（尤其是Lorraine芯片组）在多媒体处理能力上的肯定，认为其具备成为IBM多媒体解决方案的潜力。

• 市场时机：DrNosferatu指出，在PCjr失败的关键时刻，IBM急需一个新的战略方向，而Amiga的技术可能正好契合这一需求。

• 收购决策：虽然没有直接讨论，但可以从上下文中推测出IBM在当时的决策过程中可能面临多种选择和权衡，而收购Amiga只是其中之一。

争议焦点：IBM是否错失了通过收购Amiga来挽救PCjr失败的良机，以及Amiga技术是否真的能够有效解决IBM在当时所面临的市场挑战。

The Amiga's
Original Chip Set
, code-named Lorraine, was designed by the
Amiga Corporation
during the end of the first
home video game
boom. Development of the Lorraine project was done using a
Sage IV
machine nicknamed "Agony" which had 64-kbit memory modules with a capacity of 1 mbit and a 8 MHz
CPU
.

Amiga Corp. funded the development of the Lorraine by manufacturing game controllers, and later with an initial bridge loan from
Atari Inc.
while seeking further investors. The chipset was to be used in a video game machine, but following the
video game crash of 1983
, the Lorraine was reconceived as a
multi-tasking
multi-media
personal computer.
The company demonstrated a prototype at the January 1984
Consumer Electronics Show
(CES) in
Chicago
, attempting to attract investors.

The Sage acted as the CPU, and
BYTE
described "big steel boxes" substituting for the chipset that did not yet exist.
[

The magazine reported in April 1984 that Amiga Corporation "is developing a 68000-based home computer with a custom graphics processor. With 128K bytes of RAM and a floppy-disk drive, the computer will reportedly sell for less than $1000 late this year."

of Apple, who had just introduced the

44251775.article_summary:
Amiga是一系列家用电脑，最初由Amiga公司设计和销售，后来由Commodore接手，生产时间从1985年到1994年。Amiga的原始芯片组（Lorraine）项目始于第一次家用视频游戏 boom末期，最初计划用于游戏机，但在1983年游戏业崩溃后，重新定位为多媒体个人电脑。Amiga公司通过制造游戏控制器和Atari Inc.的贷款资助该项目。1984年，Amiga在消费电子展上展示原型以吸引投资。由于行业竞争激烈，Amiga难以获得进一步投资，最终在1984年8月被Commodore以2700万美元收购。

1985年，Commodore发布了Amiga 1000，具备显著领先的图形和音频能力，售价1295美元，能够显示4096种颜色、播放8位立体声音频并同时运行多个应用程序。尽管Amiga 1000技术领先，但与Atari ST的竞争中，初期软件较少，且未获得主要连锁店和软件公司的广泛支持。《纽约时报》指出，商业用户对Amiga的先进功能并不特别在意。
44251775.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：IBM是否应该收购Amiga公司并利用其技术来拯救PCjr的失败。

不同观点：
• DrNosferatu认为，IBM本可以在PCjr失败的背景下收购Amiga，并利用Amiga的技术（如Lorraine芯片组）来开发“PCjr 2”，从而挽救市场失利。这个观点暗示IBM错失了一个潜在的转机。

• 另一种隐含的观点是，IBM可能有其他战略考量，没有选择收购Amiga。虽然没有明确表达，但可以从讨论中推测出，IBM可能认为Amiga的技术不符合其长期发展战略，或者收购成本过高。

补充讨论：
• 技术匹配度：评论中隐含了对Amiga技术（尤其是Lorraine芯片组）在多媒体处理能力上的肯定，认为其具备成为IBM多媒体解决方案的潜力。

• 市场时机：DrNosferatu指出，在PCjr失败的关键时刻，IBM急需一个新的战略方向，而Amiga的技术可能正好契合这一需求。

• 收购决策：虽然没有直接讨论，但可以从上下文中推测出IBM在当时的决策过程中可能面临多种选择和权衡，而收购Amiga只是其中之一。

争议焦点：IBM是否错失了通过收购Amiga来挽救PCjr失败的良机，以及Amiga技术是否真的能够有效解决IBM在当时所面临的市场挑战。

data.title: Low-background Steel: content without AI contamination
data.author: jgrahamc
data.article_summary: 该网站（lowbackgroundsteel.ai）创建于2023年3月，旨在汇集未受AI生成内容影响的在线资源。类似于未受核试验放射性同位素污染的“低背景钢”，该网站聚焦于2022年AI内容爆发前创建的“纯净”文本、图像和视频资源。目前包含指向ChatGPT发布前的Wikipedia数据、北极代码库、古登堡计划等资源的链接。网站鼓励用户提交其他未受污染的内容来源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成内容的影响及应对策略

不同观点：
• **gojomo**：建议在Unicode中添加新的字符范围（'planes'），专门用于AI生成内容，以确保这些内容能通过软件识别并与人类创作内容区分。这种方法可以作为一种准隐蔽通道，确保AI生成内容的披露。同时带有些许玩笑性质。
   
• **K0balt**：认为AI生成内容是向平均水平回归，对训练和人类使用都有害。建议所有AI内容应加上<AI生成内容>标签，除此之外，AI内容大多是公共危害而不是公共利益。

• **protocolture**：质疑“未受污染”数据的必要性和可行性，指出像archive.org和gutenberg等网站已经存在大量数据。同时认为LLM输出最终会广泛渗透到各个领域，无法避免。

• **Legend2440**：认为长期来看，AI应从实际经验中学习，而不是从文本数据中学习，这样既能提供非版权保护的训练数据，也能避免AI污染问题。

• **ACCount36**：表示目前没有证据显示“AI污染”是AI训练中的实际问题。AI在使用不同时间段的公开数据训练时，性能差异不明显，甚至有些新数据训练的效果更好。

• **schmookeeg**：对AI内容没有特别反感，但对“未受污染”数据的比喻表示欣赏。

• **koolba**：提供了一个链接，暗示自己曾预测过相关问题。

• **nialv7**：质疑“未受污染”数据与低背景辐射钢材比喻的适用性，指出不使用AI生成内容相对容易，而制造低背景钢材则非常困难。

• **submeta**：表示已开始重新撰写“有机”内容，以避免过度修饰的AI生成文本，认为这种趋势可能会再次流行，直到LLM能生成类似的非完美文本。

• **gorgoiler**：乐观认为通过递归训练，模型可以从原始人类内容和衍生内容中提取重要特征和模式。

• **vunderba**：质疑网站横幅使用明显AI生成图像是否是故意的。

• **tomgag**：表示曾在2024年提到过低背景钢材的比喻，并提供链接。

• **Ekaros**：认为经过精心策划的内容（去除低质量和垃圾内容）仍然更有价值，并质疑大量低质量内容即使在AI之前也存在。

• **jeffchuber**：提供了一个外部链接，未在评论中详细说明观点。

• **aunty_helen**：表示2022年前创建的用户资料像是低背景钢材，自己在判断低质量内容时会查看用户资料创建时间，但常常判断错误。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于AI生成内容的识别、影响及其对数据质量和训练的潜在污染问题。
- 比喻“低背景钢材”被多次引用，用以讨论“未受污染”数据的价值和可行性。
- 不同用户对AI生成内容的看法各异，有人担忧其危害，有人认为可控或不严重。
- 实际经验与文本数据在AI训练中的价值也被讨论，认为实际经验可能提供更好的训练效果。

44239481.article_content:
Somehow I forgot to blog my site:
https://lowbackgroundsteel.ai/
. I created it back in March 2023 as a clearinghouse for online resources that hadn't been contaminated with AI-generated content.
Low-background Steel
(and lead) is a type of metal uncontaminated by radioactive isotopes from nuclear testing. That steel and lead is usually recovered from ships that sunk before the Trinity Test in 1945. The site is about uncontaminated content that I'm terming "Low-background Steel". The idea is to point to sources of text, images and video that were created prior to the explosion of AI-generated content that occurred in 2022.
It currently contains pointers to a Wikipedia dump from prior to the release of ChatGPT, the Arctic Code Vault, Project Gutenberg, and more.
If you know of other sources of non-contaminated content plus
submit them
!

data.title: TV Fool: See OTA channels you can receive
data.author: nvahalik
data.article_summary: 该网站提供多种工具和服务，帮助用户分析和查找电视及FM广播信号。主要功能包括电视信号定位、在线电视地图、Google Earth电视地图、呼号查询、信号分析和覆盖图常见问题解答等。此外，网站设有论坛和反馈渠道，方便用户交流和报告数据错误。用户可以通过这些工具获取详细的信号信息和地图数据，以改善电视和广播接收效果。网站还包含新闻和常见问题解答，帮助用户更好地理解和使用其服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个特定网站或工具的准确性、数据更新情况以及适用范围的评价

不同观点：
• [aidenn0] 认为该网站考虑了地形因素，可能比其他工具更准确，但实际使用中发现其列出的可接收频道数量与现实不符。他指出，自己处于山谷地带，实际接收不到任何频道，而网站却列出了5个“绿色”频道。此外，他质疑该网站使用的是电视台的授权有效辐射功率（ERP）而非实际ERP，并给出了一个VHF电视台的例子，其实际ERP只有100W，但网站上却列为300W。

• [iqfareez] 关注该工具的适用范围，询问其在哪些国家可以使用。这表明他对该工具的地理适用性有所关心，可能在考虑其是否适用于自己所在的地区。

• [johng] 对该网站的数据更新情况表示失望，指出其数据库自2017年以来未更新，尽管他承认该网站本身很不错。这反映出他对工具的功能和设计表示认可，但对数据更新不及时感到不满。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是网站数据的准确性，特别是关于地形影响和ERP的计算。aidenn0提供了具体的例子来支持他的质疑。
• 另一个值得注意的点是工具的数据更新频率，johng的评论指出了这一问题，可能影响用户对工具的信任和使用体验。
• iqfareez的问题引出了一个潜在的限制，即该工具的地理适用范围，这可能影响其在全球用户中的普及和使用。

data.title: Show HN: The Roman Industrial Revolution that could have been
data.author: miki_tyler
data.article_summary: 《Lydian Stone》系列漫画讲述了考古学生Ulyses意外通过一块神秘石碑与古罗马奴隶Marcus跨时空交流的故事。每一期中，Marcus面临不同的困境，Ulyses利用现代知识帮助他解决问题，逐渐改变古罗马的历史进程，推动其走向工业革命。然而，这些变化也引发了社会紧张和冲突。在第一期中，Ulyses发现石碑，与Marcus建立联系，面临是否干预历史的艰难抉择。第二期中，Marcus和主人Gaius在庞贝毁灭后利用蒸汽技术拯救社区经济。第三期将讲述Campania因拒绝奴隶制和引入火药而陷入与罗马帝国的冲突。漫画通过AI辅助创作，保留实验性错误以保持独特风格。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一部以罗马为背景的工业革命概念漫画的可行性、历史合理性以及创作方式的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持并感兴趣的观点**：
  - ilinx：对该概念表示强烈兴趣，尤其希望看到复杂技术背后的发展过程，如蒸汽机的实现及其所需的工艺细节。虽然不确定历史合理性，但认为仅作为概念非常有趣，愿意阅读。
  - adrianmonk：提到类似的故事（如Reddit上的“Rome, Sweet Rome”），表明对这种跨时代技术引入历史情境的题材有兴趣。

• **反对或质疑的观点**：
  - jcranmer：详细分析罗马工业革命的不可能性，指出罗马缺乏必要的技术基础（如精密工程）和经济结构来支持工业革命。认为将现代技术引入古代罗马在历史和社会层面上存在许多不合理之处。
  - satvikpendem：引用YouTube频道ToldInStone的视频，支持罗马不可能发生工业革命的观点，但对漫画的创作表示喜欢。

• **对AI参与创作的批评**：
  - tene80i：不认同由AI辅助创作的作品，认为创意作品应完全由人类创作，强调人类创作的独特性和情感连接。虽然理解AI可以帮助缺乏技能的人创作，但认为这降低了作品的真实性和挑战性。

• **提及类似作品**：
  - ilamont：提到Robert Silverberg的作品《Roma Eterna》，该作品涉及罗马文明发展到火箭时代的情节。
  - Tagbert：提到S.M. Stirling的小说《To Turn the Tide》，该故事涉及现代技术引入古罗马时代的情节。
  - ggm：提到L. Sprague De Camp的《Lest Darkness Fall》，这是另一部涉及时间旅行和历史技术引入的作品。

补充讨论：
• **对创作质量和AI参与度的质疑**：
  - don-code：对网站RSS feed中的内容质量表示怀疑，认为有垃圾信息的迹象。
  - notavalleyman：直接询问第一期PDF中人类创作与ChatGPT生成内容的比例，对作品的视觉一致性提出质疑。

• **对技术实现的期待**：
  - Animats：表示希望看到如何用罗马技术实现一个真正的蒸汽机，而不是玩具版的蒸汽机。

争议焦点：
- 罗马工业革命的历史合理性以及现代技术引入古代背景的可行性是主要争议点。一方认为这种设定很有趣且值得探索，另一方则认为在技术、经济和社会结构上都不具备可行性。

44253083.article_content:
NOTE:
I’ve intentionally left some obvious mistakes, like the faces on page 20 of Issue #1, to keep the raw, experimental feel of the project. As explained in the
"the making of"
section, this comic book was created with the aid of an AI model. I review and adjust each image, sometimes editing by hand to fix things like missing characters, extra fingers, or elements that don’t belong. Then I add the dialogue boxes.
I understand that newer model versions may produce better results; however, replacing the original sketches would undermine the purpose of the experiment. For each issue, I’ll use whichever LLM version is available at the time I’m working on it.
The Lydian Stone Series
The Lydian Stone is a story about an archaeology student named Ulyses who accidentally finds himself texting a Roman slave named Marcus. With each issue, Marcus faces a new danger or challenge, and Ulyses tries to help him using modern knowledge and technology, carefully adapting solutions Marcus can actually build with what's available around him. Every problem they solve together quietly sets ancient Rome on the path toward an industrial revolution, unlocking new ideas and inventions that quickly ripple through society. But as Rome rushes forward, these rapid changes create tension and trouble among people unprepared for a world transforming before their eyes. It's a story about what could have happened if history took a different path, told through friendship, ingenuity, and unintended consequences.
Issue #1 -
Contact
READ HERE
In this first issue, we meet Ulyses, a worn-down archaeology student digging in the dust of Pompeii, desperate to find something meaningful. Instead, he uncovers something impossible, a stone that bridges two timelines. Suddenly he's speaking with Marcus, an educated slave who lives just days before the city is doomed by fire and ash. As their connection grows, Ulyses faces a painful choice: intervene to save Marcus, knowing it could destroy the present as he knows it, or stand by and watch history unfold.
Issue #2 - The Engine Of Empire
COMING SOON!
In issue #2, The Engine of Empire, Marcus and his master, Gaius, find themselves facing disaster after Pompeii’s destruction. With their wool workers dead or injured, the entire Campania region is sliding toward ruin and starvation. Desperate for a solution, Marcus turns to Ulyses, whose modern knowledge helps him unlock the power of steam. Together, they create machines that weave wool without human hands, replacing the lost workers and rescuing their community. Soon they realize steam can also drive their boats, helping them deliver wool goods faster and farther than ever before.
Issue #2 - Civil War
COMING SOON!
In issue #3, Civil War, Marcus and Gaius have turned Campania into an economic powerhouse thanks to their steam-driven empire. But their success draws the eyes of Rome’s leaders, who start taxing them heavily and see their refusal to use slave labor as a dangerous threat. Tensions grow, much like those that sparked revolution in early America, dividing the empire between old traditions and new ideas. When Campania boldly outlaws slavery, the emperor orders Gaius arrested, pushing Marcus to a breaking point. Desperate and out of options, Marcus again asks Ulyses for help, and this time, with great hesitation, Ulyses introduces them to gunpowder.

data.title: Amiga 4000T: The Best Amiga in the World
data.author: codewiz
data.article_summary: Amiga 4000T被誉为最出色的Amiga电脑，是经典Amiga系列的终极产品。尽管Commodore之前已推出A3000的塔式版本，但A4000T凭借其独特的模块化和扩展性脱颖而出。该电脑由Commodore设计，但因公司1994年破产，资产被德国公司Escom收购，大多数现存的A4000T由Escom生产，数量稀少。A4000T具备68040 CPU，可扩展至68060，内存可从最低配置的2MB芯片RAM和4MB快速RAM扩展至1.7GB。它独特之处在于同时支持SCSI和IDE接口，这在当时非常罕见。虽然最初由Commodore制造的A4000T极少，但Escom版本仍具收藏价值。文章作者购买的A4000T虽功能正常，但内部凌乱，经过清理和更换硬盘后得以修复。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga 4000T及其相关Amiga电脑的特性、历史和影响

不同观点：
• **gbraad的观点**：Amiga 4000T看起来像是一台普通的商品机，与Amiga系列的其他机型差异较大，尤其是与更像Unix工作站的A3000T相比。4000T因为内部SCSI接口和扩展空间而被视为高端产品，但由于价格昂贵，市场表现不佳。另外，4000T的机箱是重新利用的PC机箱，且由于Commodore的破产，该机型生产数量非常有限（仅100-200台），现存数量极少，被认为是稀有的家用计算机。

• **neom的观点**：Amiga 4000的推出表明Amiga公司当时已经陷入困境。neom认为Windows NT和Windows 95的崛起加速了Amiga的衰落，Amiga退出市场是不可避免的。同时，提到如果GNOME和KDE没有竞争，Linux可能会有更大机会在当时成为主流。

• **flohofwoe的观点**：认为Amiga 3000是最好的Amiga机型，4000系列虽然更快，但3000在外观上更具吸引力，而4000T看起来像一台无名的PC，缺乏特色。

• **CobrastanJorji的观点**：质疑Amiga 4000T设计中的锁机制，为什么不响应鼠标移动或键盘输入但响应鼠标点击，猜测是否存在某种特定使用场景或设计缺陷。

• **trembolram的观点**：提到Atari ST在低延迟MIDI方面的优势，现代PC在这方面开箱即用不如老机器，并质疑Amiga是否有类似现代PC无法实现的功能（Amiga本身不带MIDI功能）。

• **fractallyte的观点**：提到MacroSystem的DraCo，作为Amiga 4000T的克隆机型，省略了一些Amiga芯片组，专注于非线性视频编辑，是一种高度专业化的机器，比4000T更为稀有。

• **Razengan的观点**：提议复兴1980年代的家用计算机形态，设计一种全尺寸键盘、非超薄、多接口、可拆卸显示屏的便携式桌面电脑，并希望操作系统能开箱即用，适合编程和创作，重新唤起新一代对计算机的热情。

• **orionblastar的观点**：提到AmigaOne系列，指出Amiga品牌并未完全消失，AmigaOne是现代Amiga系列的一部分，延续了Amiga的传统。

补充讨论：
- Amiga 4000T的稀有性和历史背景是讨论的核心，尤其是其生产数量少和市场表现不佳的原因。
- 不同型号Amiga之间的比较，特别是3000和4000系列在外观和功能上的差异。
- 关于现代PC与老式Amiga及其他80年代计算机在特定功能（如MIDI）上的差距。
- 对未来计算机形态的设想和期望，尤其是对复古设计的兴趣和现代操作系统的易用性。

争议焦点：Amiga 4000T的设计和市场定位是否合理，以及其与Windows等其他操作系统的竞争中失败的原因。

44253804.article_content:
Amiga 4000T: The Best Amiga in the World
Deep dive into Escom's Amiga 4000 Tower
There had never been an Amiga better than Amiga 4000T. The
T
stands for
t
ower, but this computer did not stand out in Amiga history due to its format factor, as Commodore had already been selling the tower version of A3000. Rather, it was the ultimate Amiga in what many call today the "classic" series, and nothing better — or anything else for that matter — has ever been produced in the classic Amiga line since this model was released. Let us take a deep dive into what one of the first reviewers in 1994, the year when it was released, called "the mother of all Amigas" and appreciate some of its unique features.
If you prefer watching to reading, a very detailed video covering large parts of what has been covered in this article (plus more) can be found in the YouTube video below.
Legacy
The computer was still designed by the original Commodore company, and prototypes were shown in 1993, but Commodore istelf managed to sell very few of them before they went banktrupt in May 1994. The company's assets were incorporated, under the new name Amiga Technologies, into a German home computer manufacturer Escom. That is also when Amiga computers changed their logos to this one:
Figure 1. Amiga gets a new logo.
Only a few, maybe a few dozen original Commodore-made 4000 towers exist, and hence have become rare collector items. Most of Amiga 4000Ts which we see today were made by Escom. While they are still relatively rare, based on interviews given by Petro Tyschtschenko, the head of Amiga Technologies, we can estimate that Escom sold between 5,000 and 20,0000 Amigas 4000T, with more likelihood that the actual number falls somewhere on the lower side of that range. We also know that even though the UK market was by far the most interesting one for the A1200 which Escom was also selling, the towers seemed to have been sold mostly in the US and German markets. The difficulty in estimating the actual number of units sold stems from the fact that by 1996 Escom themselves had already fallen into financial problems, and most of the information found is about their expectations and hopes to sell the towers rather than the actual numbers sold. When Escom, in turn, was selling Amiga assets to another buyer, this time to VIS corp, a configuration with 040 CPU and a 1GB drive cost USD 2700 on the retail market which translates to today's USD 5100.
The A4000 tower I purchased was in working condition, but not the cleanest and also quite messy inside. The front fan stopped working, the CPU fan fell off, and in the cobweb of cables many plugs came loose. Everything inside was covered in dust. It seems the machine had been expanded with various components until the late nineties, but after that it was left untouched until I acquired it in 2022. One thing that stood out immediately was the hard disk. The aftermarket 8.1 gigabyte Seagate SCSI drive was so loud, that I immediately decided to replace it with a quieter option, a CF card. SCSI disks were considered reliable and fast in the 90s, but that is not the case anymore a quarter of a century later.
Figure 2. A4000T prototype revealed by Commodore in 1993 (source: Aminet), and the Escom version of the computer refurbished by this article's author.
However, since the disk contained a working Workbench system, configured to perfection by the original owner, I first made a copy of it using
TSgui
, an Amiga partition and disk copying tool. Even though the system was localized into German, it seemed wrong to just leave all those meticulously edited
S:Startup-Sequence
and
S:User-Startup
files on a device which is likely to become unrecoverable very soon. SCSI drives are decades old by now, and from experience I can tell you they are the first thing to cause problems next to burst batteries and capacitors.
Specs
Let's look at the specs first: in the minimum shipped configuration it had a 68040 CPU, 2Mb of chip RAM and 4Mb of fast RAM. The CPU was expandable to 060, and fast RAM to 18Mb using modules inserted into the motherboard, or up to 1.7Gb using expansion boards. These specs were not much different from the desktop A4000, so what made the A4000T so unique? It was the modularity and expandability. Following the A3000 which had a built-in SCSI interface, and then A4000 which had a built-in IDE interface, A4000T was the only Amiga which had both of these storage device interfaces available right on the motherboard. In mid nineties SCSI harddrives were competing with their IDE counterparts in speed and reliability, but even in the PC world hardly any manufacturer supported both interfaces directly on the motherboard; most commonly attaching a SCSI required installing an additional controller card. Professional and power Amiga users at whom A4000T was targeted had the unique opportunity to take avail — right after unboxing their computer — of the cheaper IDE drives, the more expensive but faster SCSI drives,

data.title: Bliss – The story behind one of the most famous photographs (2012)
data.author: susam
data.article_summary: 《我是马丁·帕尔》（I Am Martin Parr）是一部由李·舒尔曼（Lee Shulman）执导的 intimate 纪录片，深入探讨了英国著名摄影师马丁·帕尔的生活与作品。影片通过展示帕尔的摄影历程和个人经历，揭示了他对社会、文化和日常生活的独特视角。文章作者彼得·登奇（Peter Dench）参加了该片在伦敦的首映，并对影片及帕尔的艺术成就进行了进一步了解。影片为观众呈现了一个既有深度又富有人情味的摄影大师形象。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某张图片的评价及其文化影响

不同观点：
• [metalman的观点] 认为该图片没有给人留下深刻印象，属于不对称影响（asymmetric influence）的例子。他指出该图片并不著名，也没有引起人们的注意，甚至将其描述为“ubiquitous grot”（无处不在的糟粕）。Metalman个人没有认出这张图片，除非有注释说明，并认为所有被强加的“选项”都是试图将一切制度化的证据。他质疑是否真的有粉丝基础存在，并暗示这种现象是试图将一切纳入制度化的一部分。

• [esafak的观点] 认为该图片看起来不真实，因为其色彩过于饱和且曝光过度，特别是云层部分。他不认为这是一张好照片，因为没有任何细节能吸引人的注意力，尤其不能理解它为何能作为Windows桌面背景图片使用多年。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于该图片为何能广泛传播并长期使用，尽管两位评论者都对图片的质量和影响力持怀疑态度。
- Metalman提到了图片被制度化和强加于用户的观点，暗示了对这种文化现象的批评。
- Esafak则从技术角度（如饱和度和曝光）对图片质量进行了评价，认为其缺乏吸引力。
- 两者都对该图片作为长期桌面背景的选择表示不理解，但各自的论据不同：一个是从文化和制度角度，另一个是从技术和美学角度。

data.title: Unveiling the EndBOX – A microcomputer prototype for EndBASIC
data.author: jmmv
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款名为EndBOX的怀旧计算机，其设计目标是重现过去简单直接的编程体验。EndBOX启动后直接进入EndBASIC环境，专为喜欢探索和学习编程的“黑客”及教育工作者设计，尤其适合那些怀念老式计算机的人。设备配有小屏幕而非键盘，用户可自由选择输入设备如键盘、手柄等。目前有两款原型：标准型配备7英寸触屏，基于Raspberry Pi 3B+；微型版则使用128x128 LCD，基于Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W。EndBOX运行定制的EndBOX OS，基于NetBSD，支持USB和Wi-Fi，且具抗断电特性。文章呼吁读者支持这一项目，帮助其实现批量生产。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于使用BASIC编程语言和硬件平台在教育和开发中的应用]

不同观点：
• [abraxas] 认为在专用硬件上运行快速的BASIC语言是教授孩子和初学者编程的绝佳方式。他提到这种方法类似于Maximite系列硬件及其BASIC克隆，并希望这种设置能够进入学校系统，成为像BBC Micro在英国那样的标准教学平台。

• [nopakos] 对硬件的视觉元素（如颜色、字体、Ready提示符）感到怀旧，联想到自己小时候使用的Amstrad CPC，表达了对这种复古风格的欣赏。

• [dshacker] 对WIFI驱动程序的编程表示好奇，询问如何从BASIC开始创建WIFI驱动程序，并对是否使用BASIC语言进行驱动开发提出疑问。

• [90s_dev] 认为使用像Pick 9那样的GUI开发环境可能会更好，对仅使用BASIC表示疑问，暗示可能有更现代或更直观的选择。

补充讨论：
• [_sbrk] 提供了一个链接，指向关于CH32V003芯片的讨论，可能与当前讨论的硬件平台有关，提供了进一步的技术资源。

争议焦点：
• 争议的焦点在于使用BASIC和专用硬件是否是最佳的教学和开发方式，特别是在现代技术快速发展的背景下，以及是否有更现代的GUI开发环境可以替代。

44253065.article_content:
Published on: June 6, 2025
Remember when turning a computer on meant instantly jumping into code? No bloat, no distractions—just you and a prompt? That’s the experience I’ve been working to bring back with the EndBOX: a small, resilient, nostalgia-packed, all-screen computer that boots straight into the retro-inspired EndBASIC environment you already know.
And today, six months after its inception, I’m excited to formally show you the first working prototypes—though they are still rough and need refinement. Let’s dive into the goals for the EndBOX and what it could become with your help.
💾 Sponsor the EndBOX
Who is the EndBOX for?
First and foremost, the EndBOX is for the hacker types: those of you who love tinkering with systems, languages, and hardware. But more specifically, the EndBOX caters to those who grew up with simpler computers and know that, to truly understand the fundamentals of computing, you have to experience them from the ground up with as few layers of abstraction as possible.
That said, EndBASIC has always been about providing a learning tool for coding. That was my original goal when I set out to create this language, and that goal is still very much alive. So… the EndBOX can also cater to educators as an all-in-one platform to teach kids how to program through a toy that feels personal.
What makes the EndBOX special?
The EndBOX is intended to be a small, portable device that bundles:
an embedded computer board,
a tablet-sized screen, and
a slim OS that boots straight into EndBASIC.
Why a screen and not a keyboard though? After all, old BASIC machines from the 1980s bundled the computer into the keyboard and let you supply the TV—I mean monitor. Personally, I feel this is not the best form factor in this day and age of touch screens. I want the device to feel playful. And I want to give you the freedom to connect different input peripherals as you see fit.
Put another way: the EndBOX aims to offer a standalone device that can run EndBASIC programs—and how you interact with them, be it via a keyboard, a mouse, a touch screen, a game pad, or even GPIO-attached inputs… should be up to you. In fact, some programs may not need input at all!
Concept of the EndBOX with two SNES-like USB gamepads. EndBASIC does not yet support gamepad input, but it will.
What hardware will the EndBOX have?
Right now, I have built two different EndBOX prototypes:
The standard model
, which sports a 7" HDMI touch display, USB ports, and a GPIO port (which is usable from EndBASIC but not easily accessible in this build). The current prototype is based on the
Raspberry Pi 3B+
, but future builds will likely use a smaller board for a thinner profile.
The prototype of the EndBOX I.
The micro model
, which sports a tiny 128x128 LCD and a micro USB port. The current prototype is based on the
Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W
.
The prototype of the EndBOX I Micro.
Both models provide Wi-Fi to access the EndBASIC cloud file sharing service and should (eventually) also support Bluetooth for peripheral connectivity.
What OS will the EndBOX run?
The EndBOX will run, for lack of a better name, the EndBOX OS. This OS is a quick-to-boot disk image, built on
NetBSD
, that just exposes EndBASIC. The primary goal behind the OS is get you to a prompt as quickly as possible while offering “advanced” features like USB input and Wi-Fi connectivity. A secondary goal is to be resilient to power cuts: you should be able to yank power and reboot the machine at any time to get back to a known-good state, just like you used to do.
The EndBASIC shell is a fork of EndBASIC that integrates with
NetBSD’s console framebuffer
and
other hardware interfaces
, and that provides a mechanism to control the machine from within the EndBASIC interpreter. In particular, the system exposes a
CONFIG.BAS
configuration file—inspired by MS-DOS’s
CONFIG.SYS
—to tune the behavior of the machine (such that you can, for example, modify the font used by the console or configure Wi-Fi networks).
The default configuration file with an override for the
console
setting to select a yellow-on-blue console and a larger font.
Want to help? Here’s how!
While I have a prototype in my hands, I cannot provide one to you just yet. Distributing electronics is a tricky business, and to do it correctly I need to make a plan and deal with various legalities. Plus, depending on scale, I’ll have to figure out production since, for now, I only know
how to build
a limited number of units.
So what I’m wondering today is whether YOU feel this is worth pursuing at all. The EndBOX isn’t just a computer—it’s a philosophy. It’s about computing that’s transparent, approachable, and fun. It’s about helping the next generation fall in love with programming the way we did: by typing on a real machine, with no distractions, and watching code come alive instantly.
Sounds crazy? Yes, it sure does! And
that’s why I need your support
. Here is what you can do:

data.title: Type-based vs. Value-based Reflection
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了C++26中基于值和基于类型的反射机制，重点比较了两者如何解决特定问题，即判断一个类型是否为C++20引入的“结构类型”。基于类型的反射模型由Reflection TS（技术规范）引入，使用`reflexpr(E)`运算符获取唯一类型，并通过模板元函数进行查询操作。文章详细介绍了Reflection TS的设计，包括如何使用反射类型和对象序列，并展示了如何用基于值的反射模型（C++26设计）实现类似的功能。作者通过宏定义和类型列表实现了反射操作符和对象序列，并简化了概念以保持一致性。这篇文章旨在帮助读者理解两种反射模型的差异和工作原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对C++复杂性的不同看法以及与其他编程语言的对比

不同观点：
• [naruhodo的观点] 作为一名有33年经验的C++开发者，他认为C++的某些方面过于复杂，尤其在与其他语言如Lisps或Zig对比时。他暗示这些语言在处理某些问题时可能更简洁。

• [90s_dev的观点] 他调侃地建议naruhodo写一本高质量的C++书籍，暗示这种简洁性的内容如果成书将会很畅销，可能认为市场上缺乏对C++简化诠释的优质资源。

补充讨论：
- naruhodo可能基于其长期使用C++的经验，体会到C++在某些应用场景下的复杂性，并认为其他语言如Lisps或Zig在这些方面表现更优。
- 90s_dev的观点带有些许幽默感，但也反映出对C++相关资源的期待，可能认为现有资料在简化C++复杂性方面尚有不足。
- 争议的焦点在于C++的复杂性是否可以通过更好的资源或教学来缓解，还是本质上其设计导致某些任务不如其他语言简洁。

44227649.article_content:
Type-based vs Value-based Reflection
Contents
Type-based vs Value-based Reflection
Frequently, whenever the topic of Reflection comes up, I see a lot of complains specifically about the new syntax being added to support Reflection in C++26. I’ve always thought of that as being largely driven by unfamiliarity — this syntax is new, unfamiliar, and thus bad. I thought I’d take a different tactic in this post: let’s take a problem that can only be solved with Reflection and compare what the solution would look like between:
the C++26 value-based model
the Reflection Technical Specification (TS)’s type-based model
Don’t worry if you’re not familiar with the Reflection TS, I’ll go over it in some detail shortly.
But first, today’s problem. C++20 introduced the concept of
structural type
. These are the kinds of types that you can use as
non-type
constant template parameters. The definition of
structural type
is:
A
structural type
is one of the following:
a scalar type, or
an lvalue reference type, or
a literal class type with the following properties:
all base classes and non-static data members are public and non-mutable and
the types of all base classes and non-static data members are structural types or (possibly multidimensional) arrays thereof.
There is no trait for this in the standard library today. How would we write one? Without reflection, this isn’t implementable. The first two bullets are easy, but even the most clever Boost.PFR tricks don’t do anything to help with the third. Let’s see how it’s done.
The Reflection TS
The Reflection TS (whose draft you can find
here
) was published in March, 2020. It came from the work done by Matúš Chochlík, Axel Naumann, and David Sankel in
P0194
.
The design was a
type-based
model. It introduced a new operator,
reflexpr(E)
, which gave you a
unique
type. What I mean by unique is that
reflexpr(A)
and
reflexpr(B)
are the same type if and only if
A
and
B
are the same entity.
That is the only new part of the language, which only yields types. The library side includes a bunch of template metafunctions to use for queries. For instance, the first example in the paper is, of course, enum-to-string:
enum E { first, second };
using E_m = reflexpr(E);
using namespace std::experimental::reflect;
using first_m = get_element_t<0, get_enumerators_t<E_m>>;
std::cout << get_name_v<first_m> << std::endl; // prints "first"
This example also demonstrates the other important concept to point out in the Reflection TS: what is
get_enumerators_t<E_m>
? In TS terms, that is called an
object sequence
(whereas
E_m
is just an
object
). An object sequence is basically a typelist of objects — except that they’re not strictly specified as such (and in the one implementation of the TS that I’m aware of, they’re not implemented as such either). Instead, the TS came with other metafunctions to manipulate them.
That’s basically the design in a nutshell:
reflexpr(E)
gives you a unique type representing properties of
E
the library comes with a lot of queries on reflection types
some of those queries return values (like
get_name_v
), some return types — which can be reflection types (like
get_element_t
), and some return object sequences (like
get_enumerators_t
).
On the whole, the above should be fairly familiar. It’s regular template metaprogramming. It’s simple.
Implementing the Reflection TS
It occurred to me recently that I could actually implement the Reflection TS on top of the
p2996 design
. I’m not going to implement the whole thing, I will instead do just enough to solve the problem I posed at the beginning of this blog post. But I’ll walk through how to do that, which should help shine light both on how the TS works and how the p2996 design works.
To start with, we need a reflection operator which returns a unique type per entity. We can do that with a macro:
namespace std::reflect {
template <meta::info R>
struct Reflection {
static constexpr auto value = R;
};
#define reflexpr(E) ::std::reflect::Reflection<^^E>
}
In the value-based reflection model,
^^E
gives us a unique value for each entity, with uniqueness defined exactly how we need it. So we simply need to lift that into a type.
The other fundamental piece we need is an object sequence, which I will just just implement as a type-list (even though, as mentioned, it’s not specified as such):
namespace std::reflect {
template <class... R>
struct Sequence { };
}
So far so good.
Next, the Reflection TS introduced a lot of
concept
s (it was introduced at the same time as Concepts in C++20) to help make it easier understand the API and catch invalid uses as early as possible.
The root concept is
Object
, which represents a reflection object, and everything else builds on top of that. There was also
ObjectSequence
, for object sequences. For some reason,
ObjectSequence
refined
Object
. I’m not sure why that’s helpful, since these are distinct kinds — so for simplicity I’m not going to do that, but otherwise I’m going to try to keep changes

data.title: The curious case of shell commands, or how "this bug is required by POSIX" (2021)
data.author: wonger_
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了在Linux和UNIX系统中使用诸如`bash`、`ssh`、`i3`、`screen`、`tmux`、`dtach`等工具时，它们通常依赖`system(3)`函数通过`sh -c`执行命令，而不是直接调用`execve(2)`。这种设计可能导致安全问题，特别是在处理用户输入时，未经过滤的输入可能引发shell注入风险。文章提醒开发者在编写脚本和工具时需谨慎处理命令和参数，进行适当的转义和引用，以避免潜在的安全漏洞。尽管这个问题在多个操作系统的工具中普遍存在，但相关文档如POSIX手册中并未充分强调这一风险，因此开发者需格外注意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：命令行选项和代码执行的安全性问题，特别是在不同操作系统和编程语言中处理命令行参数时的潜在风险。

不同观点：
• **panzi的观点**：认为`system()`应该被弃用，推荐使用`exec*()`和`posix_spawn()`。同时指出Windows下每个程序可能会不同地解析命令行字符串，并提到Rust对该问题有警告，而Java则没有。
• **o11c的观点**：认为将命令传递给shell有时是必要的功能，比如`popen("gzip > foo.gz")`。强调无论使用哪个API，都应该对用户输入进行清理。对`ssh`的批评表示不满，认为实际问题被文章中的其他内容掩盖了。
• **chubot的观点**：指出`ssh`和`eval`的内置函数在处理参数时存在问题，建议使用类似`quote-argv()`的函数来正确引用参数。还提到Oils shell可能会引入一个新的`invoke`内置函数来解决这个问题。
• **endiangroup的观点**：介绍了自己写的工具`cmdjail`，用于限制`ssh`命令的执行，但承认工具仍可能存在问题，因为底层使用了shell命令。
• **1vuio0pswjnm7的观点**：讨论了`bash`和`dash`等不同shell的性能和使用场景，指出Debian等系统不使用`bash`作为默认的shell脚本解释器。
• **blueflow的观点**：指出命令和参数向量是不同的概念，认为作者在文章中混淆了这两个概念。
• **a_t48的观点**：建议尽量避免在程序中调用shell命令，推荐使用Python的`shlex.quote`函数来解决参数引用问题。
• **hackernudes的观点**：认为文章难以 follow，但认可`${var@Q}`和`printf '%q'`作为解决方案，希望有更明显的方法来处理嵌套的`sh -c`调用。

补充讨论：
• 对不同编程语言和操作系统的比较，特别是Rust和Java在处理命令行参数时的差异。
• 提供了多个实际的例子和解决方案，如`quote-argv()`函数和`cmdjail`工具。
• 争议的焦点在于是否应该完全弃用`system()`以及如何在不同场景下安全地执行命令行操作。
• 对shell命令和参数处理的细节进行了深入讨论，特别是如何正确引用和转义参数以避免安全问题。

44236241.article_content:
Some context
(For those interested only in the
glibc
and POSIX issues, see
at the end
.)
I use Linux almost everywhere, from laptops and desktops to servers and routers, and over the course of many years I've written quite a few
bash
scripts that ease my interaction with all of these.
The usual "stack" that ties all of these together is composed of:
bash
, obviously for scripting;
ssh
, for remote execution;
i3
, the window manager for desktop environments;
screen
, for terminal multiplexing;
tmux
, for terminal multiplexing;
dtach
, for launching processes in background while still being able to access them if needed;
(among many other tools like
coreutils
and friends,
grep
,
sed
,
sort
,
find
,
xargs
,
rsync
, plus other smaller C, Go or Rust based tools; but all of these are not the subject of this article;)
What do all of the former have in common? They all provide some sort of functionality, but by themselves they don't actually do anything; they are meant to delegate the actual work to other tools.
So what is the problem you ask? Nothing really... Everything is fine... No planes are falling from the sky... Nobody is running around screaming while on fire...
Everything is business as usual,
unless you want to write some wrapper scripts that takes arbitrary user input and delegates that to one of these, and many other, broken tools
...
And just for completeness I'll throw in some other tools that fit the bill:
make
(and any other variant or derivate), for build systems;
ninja
, my favorite build system, and lightweight DAG job scheduler and executer;
Root of all evil
As many of you have guessed, because we live in a UNIX world, many of these tools delegate the actual tool execution to the
glibc
system(3)
function,
which ends-up calling
sh(1p)
(most likely
bash
) with the
-c
argument.
As opposed to doing the correct thing and just calling
execve(2)
...
BTW, this is not something Linux specific. Unfortunately it is a trait inherited from the UNIX ancestry by almost all operating systems, including all BSD variants plus OSX;
and, for some tools, this behavior is even seen when running on Windows.
But I digress...
Excerpts from Linux
system(3)
man page
Let's quote from the Linux
system(3)
man page:
The
system(3)
library function uses
fork(2)
to create a child
process that executes the shell command specified in command
using
execl(3)
as follows:
execl("/bin/sh", "sh", "-c", command, (char *) NULL);
[...]
Any user input that is employed as part of command should be
carefully sanitized, to ensure that unexpected shell commands or
command options are not executed. Such risks are especially
grave when using
system()
from a privileged program.
So far the warning doesn't sound very comforting...
But hey, we are all responsible developers...
Excerpts from POSIX
system(3p)
man page
Let's quote from the POSIX
system(3p)
man page:
Hmm... Strange... There is nothing to quote from this manual about warnings, issues or sanitization...
(Except perhaps the warning for set-UID or set-GID processes against using this function, due to potential privilege escalation issues.)
Excerpts from POSIX
sh(1p)
man page
How about quoting from the POSIX
sh(1p)
man page regarding the
-c
flag:
-c
-- Read commands from the command_string operand. Set the
value of special parameter 0 (see Section 2.5.2,
Special Parameters) from the value of the command_name
operand and the positional parameters (
$1
,
$2
, and so
on) in sequence from the remaining argument operands.
No commands shall be read from the standard input.
OK... Still nothing about warnings, issues or sanitization...
Excerpts from
bash(1)
man page
Perhaps we'll have more luck quoting from the
bash(1)
man page:
-c
-- If the
-c
option is present, then commands are read from
the first non-option argument command_string. If there
are arguments after the
command_string
, the first argument
is assigned to
$0
and any remaining arguments are assigned
to the positional parameters. The assignment to
$0
sets
the name of the shell, which is used in warning and error
messages.
Hmm... Perhaps sanitization isn't that a big of an issue?
Partial conclusion
For now let's remember that initial remark:
Any user input [...] part of command should be [...] sanitized [...].
Aside from that, perhaps this "shell command" business I'm crying about isn't such a big of an issue?
Else the POSIX manuals for
system(3p)
(~2K words) and
sh(1p)
(~8K words)
-- that I assume were written by legions of committee members -- would have certainly spared at least a few words about this issue...
Right?
Unintended consequences
So why do we care about
system(3)
and
sh -c
?
Because as said in the beginning, many tools accept as arguments commands which in the end are passed to
sh -c
via the
system(3)
function.
Therefore when we write our scripts and tools we need to be aware of this situation and be prepared to escape and quote our commands and arguments accordingly,
else we'll be subject to
shell injections
... (For more sc

data.title: The Canadian C++ Conference
data.author: BiraIgnacio
data.article_summary: CppNorth是将于2025年7月20-23日在加拿大多伦多举办的C++会议。此次大会为期三天，汇集本地及外邀讲者，提供学习、交流和探索C++社区新动态的机会。讲者阵容强大，包括Scott Hanselman、Alex Dathskovsky和Kate Gregory等。JetBrains和Autodesk分别是视频和金牌赞助商。会议酒店为King Edward Hotel，现已开放购票和预订。同时招募志愿者，参与者可选择现场或组织工作。大会还提供特别优惠，预订Royal York Hotel可享受800美元折扣。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加拿大举办的C++技术会议（CppNorth）高票价是否合理及当地人如何负担

不同观点：
• [babuloseo的观点] 对于会议票价高达1500美元表示震惊，尤其在加拿大，并质疑当地人是如何负担这样高昂的费用。这暗示了票价可能过高，超出了一般参会者的承受能力。

• [BiraIgnacio的观点] 强调CppNorth大会建立在多伦多用户组的成功基础上，汇集本地和外地的演讲者，提供为期三天的学习、社交和发现C++社区新动态的机会。这表明会议具有较高的价值，可能 justify 其高票价。

补充讨论：
• CppNorth的票价问题引发对技术会议定价的讨论，特别是对当地社区参会者经济能力的关注。
• BiraIgnacio的回应暗示会议的质量和机会可能对高票价做出合理解释，但未直接回应票价是否对当地人构成负担。
• 争议焦点在于高票价是否合理，以及当地参会者如何应对这一经济压力。

data.title: Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Cellebrite UFED (2021)
data.author: s-mon
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了Cellebrite的UFED和Physical Analyzer软件中的漏洞。Cellebrite主要用于从移动设备中提取和索引数据，其客户包括一些专制政权和军事机构，曾涉及迫害记者和活动人士。文章指出，Cellebrite软件的功能是在物理持有设备的情况下，自动化提取和显示数据。其软件需要解析来自各种应用的“不受信任”数据，这使得它容易受到内存损坏等漏洞的攻击。

作者意外获得了一套Cellebrite软件，并发现其在软件安全方面缺乏防护，许多标准的安全缓解措施缺失。例如，其捆绑的FFmpeg DLLs自2012年以来未更新，存在上百个未修复的安全漏洞。通过在设备应用中包含特制文件，攻击者可以在Cellebrite机器上执行任意代码，修改扫描报告，包括插入或删除文本、照片、联系人等数据，且无检测痕迹。这显示了Cellebrite软件在安全性上的严重不足。

44253410.article_content:
Exploiting vulnerabilities in Cellebrite UFED and Physical Analyzer from an app's perspective
moxie0
on 21 Apr 2021
Cellebrite makes software to automate physically extracting and indexing data from mobile devices. They exist within the grey – where enterprise branding joins together with the larcenous to be called “digital intelligence.” Their customer list has included authoritarian regimes in Belarus, Russia, Venezuela, and China; death squads in Bangladesh; military juntas in Myanmar; and those seeking to abuse and oppress in Turkey, UAE, and elsewhere. A few months ago, they
announced that they added Signal support to their software
.
Their products have often been linked to the persecution of imprisoned journalists and activists around the world, but less has been written about what their software
actually does
or how it works. Let’s take a closer look. In particular, their software is often associated with bypassing security, so let’s take some time to examine the security of their own software.
The background
First off, anything involving Cellebrite starts with someone else physically holding your device in their hands. Cellebrite does not do any kind of data interception or remote surveillance. They produce two primary pieces of software (both for Windows): UFED and Physical Analyzer.
UFED creates a backup of your device onto the Windows machine running UFED (it is essentially a frontend to
adb backup
on Android and iTunes backup on iPhone, with some additional parsing). Once a backup has been created, Physical Analyzer then parses the files from the backup in order to display the data in browsable form.
When Cellebrite announced that they added Signal support to their software, all it really meant was that they had added support to Physical Analyzer for the file formats used by Signal. This enables Physical Analyzer to display the Signal data that was extracted from an unlocked device in the Cellebrite user’s physical possession.
One way to think about Cellebrite’s products is that if someone is physically holding your unlocked device in their hands, they could open whatever apps they would like and take screenshots of everything in them to save and go over later. Cellebrite essentially automates that process for someone holding your device in their hands.
The rite place at the Celleb…rite time
By a truly unbelievable coincidence, I was recently out for a walk when I saw a small package fall off a truck ahead of me. As I got closer, the dull enterprise typeface slowly came into focus: Cellebrite. Inside, we found the latest versions of the Cellebrite software, a hardware dongle designed to prevent piracy (tells you something about their customers I guess!), and a bizarrely large number of cable adapters.
The software
Anyone familiar with software security will immediately recognize that the primary task of Cellebrite’s software is to parse “untrusted” data from a wide variety of formats as used by many different apps. That is to say, the data Cellebrite’s software needs to extract and display is ultimately generated and controlled by the apps on the device, not a “trusted” source, so Cellebrite can’t make any assumptions about the “correctness” of the formatted data it is receiving. This is the space in which virtually all security vulnerabilities originate.
Since almost all of Cellebrite’s code exists to parse untrusted input that could be formatted in an unexpected way to exploit memory corruption or other vulnerabilities in the parsing software, one might expect Cellebrite to have been extremely cautious. Looking at both UFED and Physical Analyzer, though, we were surprised to find that very little care seems to have been given to Cellebrite’s
own
software security. Industry-standard exploit mitigation defenses are missing, and many opportunities for exploitation are present.
As just one example (unrelated to what follows), their software bundles FFmpeg DLLs that were built in 2012 and have not been updated since then. There have been
over a hundred security updates
in that time, none of which have been applied.
The exploits
Given the number of opportunities present, we found that it’s possible to execute arbitrary code on a Cellebrite machine simply by including a specially formatted but otherwise innocuous file in any app on a device that is subsequently plugged into Cellebrite and scanned. There are virtually no limits on the code that can be executed.
For example, by including a specially formatted but otherwise innocuous file in an app on a device that is then scanned by Cellebrite, it’s possible to execute code that modifies not just the Cellebrite report being created in that scan, but also
all previous and future generated Cellebrite reports
from all previously scanned devices and all future scanned devices in any arbitrary way (inserting or removing text, email, photos, contacts, files, or any other data), with no detectable timestamp changes or checksum failures. This could even be do

data.title: Microsoft Office migration from Source Depot to Git
data.author: dshacker
data.article_summary: 本文简要描述了微软将Office代码库从Source Depot迁移到Git的过程，强调了开发者生产力（DevEx）的重要性。Source Depot是微软早期自建的版本控制系统，类似于Perforce，但使用繁琐，分支创建和代码合并都非常耗时。随着时间推移，Source Depot逐渐老旧，维护成本高且无法提供现代开发技能。迁移到Git涉及数千名工程师，耗时数年，需兼顾不同客户的发布周期和版本一致性。为顺利迁移，微软设立了“开发者满意度” champions，协调各团队工作。此次迁移不仅关乎技术升级，还旨在提升开发者效率和技能更新。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软从Source Depot等旧版本控制系统（VCS）迁移到Git的相关技术挑战和经验分享

不同观点：
• **支持Git取代旧系统的观点**：[2d8a875f-39a2-4]指出，虽然Perforce和Source Depot在集中式版本控制系统时代表现出色，但技术已经发展，Git通过VFS解决了大仓库管理的问题，适应了现代需求。
• **质疑Git适应性的观点**：[airstrike]对微软使用4000名工程师维护Office表示怀疑，认为小团队也能完成类似任务，暗示Git及现代工具未必显著提升效率。
• **对迁移过程的复杂性提出疑问**：[ThinkBeat]关注Git在实际使用中的不足之处，特别是在大型项目中的仓库结构和GitLFS集成问题。
• **对Source Depot的怀旧和现状质疑**：[azhenley]提到2016年仍有开发者使用Source Depot，并对是否完全迁移到Git表示好奇。[BobbyTables2]则关注微软何时放弃Visual SourceSafe，认为其应被召回以避免继续公开发行使用。

补充讨论：
• **技术细节讨论**：[MBCook]和[palmotea]对Source Depot中的技术概念（如正向集成和反向集成）以及Source Depot与TFSVC之间的关系提出问题，显示出对技术细节的关注。
• **迁移经验分享**：[israrkhan]分享了他们从Perforce迁移到Git的经验，提到虽然面临一些问题，但无需发明类似VFS的工具，GitLFS对大文件管理很有帮助。
• **对具体技术问题的探讨**：[ksynwa]对OneNote的浅克隆为何达到200GB表示不解，反映出对具体技术实现细节的关注。[3eb7988a1663]则提到在系统迁移过程中通知不充分的问题，强调了沟通的重要性。
• **对未来SCM系统的展望**：[AdamN]提出是否还有其他SCM系统或Git是否已成为最终解决方案的疑问，反映了对版本控制系统未来发展的思考。

争议焦点：
• **Git是否完全优于旧系统**：部分评论如[2d8a875f-39a2-4]认为Git通过VFS等技术已解决大仓库管理问题，但[airstrike]则质疑Git及现代开发工具的实际效率提升。
